_meta.source: coordinate-mismatch bucket: distinct same-name beaches we lack
_meta.note: 18 distinct missing beaches (name collisions) with disambiguated names. 20 fix_our_pin + 2 borderline deferred to pin-review report.
deferred: Πλάκα (Άνδρος) — Andros curated-wind 41/41 invariant; needs manual wind override first.

beaches.verifyReason: Our record 1605 "Άμμος" (36.78818, 21.71032) is Ammos Beach on Sapientza island opposite Methoni, Messinia — the island's only sandy beach, boat-only access from Methoni/Pylos, unorganized with natural tree shade. Metadata (Sapientza cruises source, messinia.mobi, boat_only, fine/coarse sand, shade) and reverse-geocode (Methoni, Pylos-Nestor, Messenia) all confirm our pin is correctly placed near Sapientza. The OSM node 4295829608 (40.3855183, 22.6208746) is tagged natural=beach named Άμμος, located ~408 km away at Αλυκή / Pydna-Kolindros, Pieria, Central Macedonia — on the Thermaic Gulf mainland coast. This sits in the Alyki Kitrous / Skala Alykon area, which is a real, wide, sandy, shallow, swimmable beach (~250m long, partly organized with beach bars plus free sections) in Greece. The two are clearly different beaches in completely different regions (Messinia island vs Pieria mainland) sharing the generic Greek name "Άμμος" (= "sand"), a classic recurring-name collision rather than a coordinate error. The OSM beach is a distinct real Greek beach we are missing; since bare "Άμμος" collides with our existing Sapientza record, suggested name disambiguates by area (Αλυκή Κίτρους, Πιερία).

OSM way 148118878 (38.8316, 20.6699) is Agios Ioannis / Άι Γιάννης beach next to Lefkada Town, Ionian Islands: a real, public, swimmable Greek beach (natural=beach), ~3 km long, Blue Flag, and the island's premier kitesurf/windsurf spot. Our record (id 355) is a DIFFERENT Άι Γιάννης beach 207 km away in Fthiotida (mainland), near Lichada/north Evoikos gulf — verified by its own OSM node 4712250192 (natural=beach, same name) at the exact coordinates plus a verified Google placeId with 69 reviews (4.5 stars). Άι Γιάννης / Άγιος Ιωάννης is one of the most recurrent beach names in Greece (also Gavdos, Halkidiki, Crete, etc.), so these are coincidentally same-named, genuinely distinct beaches in different regions — not a coordinate split of one beach. Our Fthiotida pin is correctly placed and plausible; the Lefkada beach is a notable beach we are missing, so it should be added as a distinct record with a disambiguated name to avoid colliding with the existing Fthiotida "Άι Γιάννης".

The OSM feature (way 93887453, 39.7767/19.9547) is a real natural=beach named "Άκολη" in NORTHEAST CORFU (Ionian Islands), within the Erimitis ecosystem near Avlaki Beach / Agios Stefanos / Kassiopi. AllTrails confirms it as a real, secluded swimmable beach ("Agios Stefanos Bay - Vromolimni and Akoli Lakes - Avlaki Beach"; "secluded Akoli beach on the east coast"). It is in Greece, not Turkey/Albania, and is not a bar/hotel/marina/headland. RELATION = distinct_beach: our record is the famous Άκολη/Άβυθος beach in Achaia (Aigialeia, Rododafni) on the Gulf of Corinth, ~246 km away on the mainland — a completely different beach that merely shares the recurring Greek name. OUR PIN is correct: 38.27712/22.05292 lands exactly on the OSM natural=beach polygon "Άκολη" (way 750092119, center 38.27712/22.05292, pebblestone) ~75 m from the waterline, in the correct Άβυθος/Rododafni village confirmed by multiple sources (discoveraigialeia, allaboutpeloponnisos, aigiorama). Therefore the Corfu beach is a distinct real beach we are missing; since the bare name "Άκολη" collides with our existing Achaia record, it should be added disambiguated as "Άκολη (Κέρκυρα)".

OSM way 93887470 (39.7799, 19.9401) is Avlaki Beach in Kassiopi, NE Corfu — a real, public, swimmable pebble beach with sunbeds, tavernas and watersports, tagged natural=beach, surface=pebblestone; firmly in Greece. Our record (id 1021) is a DIFFERENT 'Αυλάκι': a SW-coast pebbly/rocky inlet on PAXOS (a separate Ionian island ~68 km south), documented by The Thinking Traveller/Paxos sources as a steep-walk-or-boat-access reef inlet near Agrilas, with verified Google placeId and 106 ratings. Our Paxos pin (39.19165, 20.16536) sits correctly on the Paxos west coast and matches all sources, so it is NOT misplaced. The two are genuinely distinct beaches that merely share the common Greek name 'Αυλάκι' (furrow/channel). The Corfu beach is a distinct real Greek beach we are missing; since the bare name collides with our Paxos record, disambiguate as Corfu/Kassiopi.

OSM way/93887480 (39.7734, 19.9554) is a real swimmable pebble cove beach named "Vromolimni Beach" in the Erimitis area of NE Corfu (Kassiopi), tagged natural=beach and confirmed by AtCorfu, Terrabook, World Beach Guide and AllTrails; it is isolated, accessed by the Erimitis path or boat, and part of a protected Ionian wetland ecosystem. Our record (id 1842) is a DIFFERENT beach 520 km away on Kimolos (Cyclades), NE coast near Prassa at 36.8318/24.59071 — described in our data as a small sulfurous/volcanic-water spot near Prassa, adjacent to the Γκιώνη record (36.8296/24.58928), with a documented Kimolos "Vromolimni" sea-cave/sulfur location. The two only share the generic Greek toponym "Βρωμολίμνη" (foul/sulfurous water), so they are distinct beaches on different islands and seas. Our Kimolos pin is coastal and on the correct island, so it is plausible and should stay; the Corfu beach is a real Greek beach we lack and would collide on the bare name, hence the disambiguated suggestedName.

Two genuinely distinct same-named beaches on Corfu, ~26.6 km apart. OUR pin (39.5466, 19.8488, lon 19.85) is the famous west-central Agios Gordios resort beach: Nominatim reverse-geocodes it directly to the "Agios Gordios" locality in the Municipality of Central Corfu, and sources confirm a 2.5km organized golden-sand beach there — our pin is correct and plausible. The OSM way 190617200 (39.3756, 20.0654, lon 20.07) reverse-geocodes to Bastatika/Paleochori in the Municipality of Southern Corfu (Lefkimmi area), the SE tip of Corfu facing the mainland — not Corfu's west coast. Sources (projectcorfu.com "Agios Gordios South", worldbeachguide, greeka) confirm a second, separate "Agios Gordis South" beach near Paleochori/Spartera/Lefkimmi: a real public, unorganized pebble-and-sand swimmable beach with clear waters, explicitly described as distinct from the west-coast resort beach. OSM tags it natural=beach, surface=sand. It is in Greece (Corfu), not Turkey/Albania. So this is a distinct real Greek beach we lack; add it with a Lefkimmi disambiguator to avoid colliding with our existing west-coast record.

Two genuinely distinct beaches share the common Greek name "Καλάμι" (reed), ~40 km apart. OUR record (39.4732, 20.24016) is the real ~200m gravel "Kalami Beach" at Plataria Bay near Igoumenitsa, Thesprotia/Epirus (mainland NW Greece) — Camping Kalami Beach GPS is 39.47417/20.24111, ~100m from our pin, so our coordinate is correct and plausible. The OSM way/42749230 (39.7435074, 19.9338657) is a DIFFERENT, famous, real public swimmable pebble/gravel beach on Corfu's NE coast: "Kalami Beach"/"Παραλία Καλάμι", the Durrell "White House" bay near Kouloura/Kassiopi, tagged natural=beach surface=gravel — clearly in Greece (Corfu, Ionian Islands), not a bar/hotel/marina/headland. Since they are different beaches in different places (Corfu island vs Epirus mainland) that merely share a name, the Corfu beach is a distinct real Greek beach we lack. The bare name collides with our existing Epirus record, so disambiguate as "Παραλία Καλάμι (Κέρκυρα)".

Both coordinates are on Ithaca, Greece, but they are two DIFFERENT beaches that share the name Φιλιατρό. (1) OUR record (38.37179, 20.74177) is the famous "Filiatro" near Vathy in southern Ithaca — Terrabook explicitly places it "in the southern part of the island, 15 min by car from Vathi" (the organized beach with beach bar, sunbeds, tree shade). Our pin is correctly placed (~south Ithaca near Vathy), so ourPinPlausible=true. (2) The OSM relation 16239697 is explicitly named "Filiatro of Kioni" (natural=beach) and sits at 38.4444, 20.6972 near Kioni village in NORTHERN Ithaca, ~9 km from our record. The Municipality of Ithaca official tourism site has a dedicated separate page "Φιλιατρό (Κιόνι)" describing it as a real public swimmable beach near the entrance of the Gulf of Kioni — pebbles/small stones, ~50 m long, semi-organized with a summer canteen plus toilet/shower, natural tree shade, car access through the village — and notes it is distinct from the main Filiatro near Vathy. Foursquare also lists "Παραλία Φιλιατρό, Κιόνι Ιθάκης" as a beach. Our dataset's existing Kioni-area beaches are Kritami, Plakoutses and the Kourvoulia coves — no Filiatro — so this northern beach is genuinely missing. Since the bare name collides with our existing Vathy record, disambiguate as "Παραλία Φιλιατρό (Κιόνι)". Confident, multi-source (official municipality site, OSM tag, Foursquare).

OSM way 237382152 (38.0708849, 20.7992981) is natural=beach named Σκάλα/Skala and reverse-geocodes to Skala village, Municipal Unit of Elios-Proni, Kefalonia, Ionian Islands, Greece. It is the well-known Skala Beach on the SE tip of Kefalonia: a large, organized, 5+ km golden-sand public swimming beach (top tourist resort, Caretta caretta nesting) — clearly real, swimmable, and in Greece, not a bar/marina/headland. Our record id 877 is a DIFFERENT Σκάλα: a small hidden pebble/grey-sand beach in the Ammoudia area of Parga Municipality, Preveza, Epirus (~130 km north), strongly supported by our own metadata (dimospargas.gr Skala/Ammoudia page, verified Google placeId, 1203 ratings @4.7). Our pin (39.21175, 20.4902) reverse-geocodes to Ammoudia, Parga Municipality, Preveza, Epirus — exactly matching the cited source — so our coordinate is plausible and correctly placed; it is NOT the same beach. This is a classic recurring-name collision: the OSM Kefalonia Skala is a distinct real Greek beach we are missing. Because the bare name "Σκάλα" collides with our existing Epirus record, the new entry should be disambiguated as Σκάλα (Κεφαλονιά).

Two different real beaches sharing the very common Greek name "Λιμνιώνας" (~106km apart, different islands). OUR record (id 2339, 36.77375/26.9628) is the Limnionas beach on KOS — a small fishing-port bay 4.5km north of Kefalos, NW Kos; our pin sits in the Limnionas hamlet of Kefalos on the bay, a correct location (ourPinPlausible=true). The OSM feature (relation 454576, 37.6933/26.6318) is "Beach Limnionas" on SAMOS (Marathokampos/Agia Kyriaki, North Aegean), tagged natural=beach: one of Samos's most famous beaches, ~350m sand+small pebbles, very calm protected bay, sunbeds/bars/restaurants — a genuine public swimmable Greek beach. So they are clearly distinct beaches, not the same bay. The Samos Limnionas is a real Greek beach we are missing; add it as a distinct record. Bare name collides with our Kos record, so disambiguate as "Λιμνιώνας (Σάμος)".

Our record (id 2012) at 37.0507, 25.3693 is the famous Plaka Beach on the WEST coast of NAXOS (Cyclades): a ~4km long sandy family beach ~8-9km SW of Naxos Town, continuation of Agia Anna. That coordinate sits exactly on the Naxos west coast at this beach, so our pin is correct/plausible. The OSM relation 454567 (natural=beach, "Plaka Beach") at 37.6989, 26.5834 is a DIFFERENT beach: a secluded, unorganized natural beach in western SAMOS (North Aegean) near Marathokampos/Paleochori, accessible via dirt road — confirmed real, swimmable, and in Greece (not Turkey/Albania). The two are ~129km apart on different islands and merely share the very common Greek beach name "Πλάκα", so they are genuinely distinct beaches, not segments of one. The Samos Plaka is a real Greek beach we lack; since "Πλάκα"/"Plaka Beach" collides with our existing Naxos record, it should be added disambiguated as "Πλάκα (Σάμος)".

Two distinct real Greek beaches sharing the common name Καλόγερος (= "monk"). OUR record (id 2081, 37.13099/24.43522) is the genuine Καλόγερος beach on Serifos (Cyclades, South Aegean): a secluded pebble beach on the southern coast between Mega Livadi and Malliadiko, accessed by a 15-20 min trail from Malliadiko or by boat (confirmed by serifos.gr, discover-serifos.com, topoguide.gr — all match our access label and pin location exactly). The OSM feature (36.5102892/22.9704615, way 1517055494, tagged natural=beach, sand) is Kalogeras beach on ELAFONISOS island (off Lakonia, Peloponnese) — a real public swimmable sandy beach on the NW edge of Elafonisos village with cedar trees, sand dunes and shallow turquoise water (confirmed by visitelafonisos.gr, greeka.com, OSM Elafonisos edit). The two are ~147 km apart in different regions, not the same beach. Our Serifos pin is correctly placed, so no fix needed; the Elafonisos beach is a distinct Greek beach we are missing. Suggested disambiguated name "Καλόγερος (Ελαφόνησος)" because the bare name collides with our existing Serifos record.

OSM way 274361086 (natural=beach, sand) centers at 36.6876, 22.8280, which reverse-geocodes to Plytra (Πλύτρα), Papadianika, Municipality of Monemvasia, Lakonia, Peloponnese, Greece. Multiple Greek travel sources (karidotsouflo.gr, lakonia.mobi, peloponnisossearch) confirm it as a real, public, golden-sand, swimmable beach near Plytra ("the exotic golden beach of Plytra"). It is in Greece, not a bar/hotel/marina/headland. Our record id 680 is a DIFFERENT beach: Karavostasi at Bali, Rethymno, Crete (35.41704, 24.78526), 225 km away, with a verified Google placeId (ChIJi6pX58mumxQRDhipPbKJaeU) and a CretanBeaches source explicitly confirming the Bali-cove identity — so our pin is correct, not misplaced. Καραβοστάσι is a common recurring Greek beach name (also exists at Oitylo/Mani, Thesprotia, Lasithi). Our dataset already has three Καραβοστάσι records (Bali-Rethymno, Lasithi 35.13/25.73, Thesprotia 39.34/20.29) but NONE in Lakonia/Plytra, so the OSM beach is a distinct real Greek beach we are missing. Because the bare name collides with existing records, the new record should be disambiguated as Καραβοστάσι (Πλύτρα).

OSM way 429820024 is tagged natural=beach named Αγία Παρασκευή at 39.8627, 22.7497, which reverse-geocodes to Στόμιο (Stomio), Δήμος Αγιάς, Larissa, Thessaly — the mainland Aegean coast. Stomio has a ~2km golden sandy public swimmable beach, and sources confirm a named "Αγία Παρασκευή" beach section/camp on the Stomio shore. So the OSM feature is a real, public, Greek beach. Our record (39.1418, 23.4389) is the well-known Αγία Παρασκευή/Πλατανιάς beach in southern Skiathos (Sporades), near Troulos/Koukounaries — a plausible, correct location for a Skiathos beach of that name. The two are ~100 km apart, on different landmasses (Skiathos island vs Larissa mainland), so they are genuinely DISTINCT beaches that merely share the very common Greek hagionym "Αγία Παρασκευή," not the same physical beach. Therefore the OSM location is a distinct real beach we are missing. Because the bare name collides with our existing Skiathos record, suggested a disambiguated name adding the village: "Αγία Παρασκευή (Στόμιο)".

OSM node 12598434867 (39.5857258, 22.9267965) is a real natural=beach "Paralia Ai Giannis", a public swimmable pebble beach near the village of Κεραμίδι (Keramidi), North Pelion, Regional Unit of Magnesia, Thessaly, Greece (confirmed via Ecotourism Greece and Wikiloc "Παραλία Αη Γιάννης Κεραμιδίου Μαγνησίας"). Not a bar/hotel/marina/headland, and clearly in Greece (mainland Pelion, Aegean coast). Our record (38.72486, 23.06106) is a DIFFERENT real beach: "Άι Γιάννης" near Λιβανάτες (Livanates), Lokrida, Phthiotis, Central Greece — a Blue Flag beach with a chapel of Saint John; Nominatim returns a natural=beach named "Άι Γιάννης" at exactly 38.7248593, 23.0610615, confirming our pin is correctly placed on land at the coast, not misplaced. The two are ~96 km apart in different regional units (Magnesia/Pelion vs Phthiotis/Lokrida) on opposite shores, so they are genuinely distinct beaches that merely share the extremely common Greek name "Άι Γιάννης" (St. John). Therefore the OSM Keramidi beach is a distinct beach we are missing; since the bare name collides with our existing Livanates record, disambiguate by adding the village/area.

Our record "Νικοτσάρα" (39.1995341, 23.490082; aliases Lechouni/Λεχουνί) is the well-documented Nikotsara/Lechouni beach on Skiathos, below Evangelistria Monastery on the NE coast. Reverse geocoding our pin returns Δήμος Σκιάθου (Καλύβια), and multiple sources (skiathos.gr, allovergreece, greeka) confirm this Skiathos beach — so our pin is plausible and correct. The OSM way 669520193 named "Lechoúni" (natural=beach) is at 39.2674236, 23.9766526, which reverse-geocodes to Δήμος Αλοννήσου, ~42km away on a DIFFERENT island. This corresponds to "Lechouni beach III", a real ~30m sandy boat-access cove on Peristera island inside the Alonissos Marine Park (confirmed by beaches-searcher.com and web sources describing Lechouni as a Marine Park swimming spot on Peristera). These are two genuinely distinct Greek beaches sharing the name "Λεχούνι" — a classic name-recurrence case, not the same physical beach. Therefore the OSM Peristera/Alonissos Lechouni is a distinct real beach we are missing; since the bare name collides with our Skiathos record's alias, disambiguate as "Λεχούνι (Περιστέρα)". Caveat: the OSM way is sloppily tagged (name in surface=Λεχούνι, only int_name set) and it is a boat-only Marine Park cove, so when added it should be marked boat-access.

OSM way 1082118806 (39.1248, 23.7296) is natural=beach, surface=stone, named Πλάκα, with an attached footway and coastline = a real, public, land-accessible swimmable pebble beach in Greece (Skopelos, Sporades). Tourist sources (skopelos.com, greeka, enjoythessaly) confirm it as the Skopelos Town/Chora beach "at the other end of the port, below the Panagitsa of Pyrgos," part of the Chora town swimming-beach group (Ammos/Abeliki/Plakes/Milos). Reverse-geocode of the OSM coord lands in Skopelos town (Alouphi / Vassileos Othonos St). This is a DISTINCT beach from our record: our Πλάκα (39.0855, 23.68) sits ~6 km away on the SOUTHWEST coast in the Panormos/Loutsa/Neo Klima area — confirmed by reverse-geocode (Λούτσα, Πάνορμος) and by its dataset neighbors Καστάνη (39.0865/23.6865), Σπηλιά and Πάνορμος, matching the documented "Πλάκα between Palio and Neo Klima near Glossa" beach. So the two are genuinely different same-named beaches on opposite sides of the island. Our pin is well placed (not misplaced), so this is not a fix_our_pin case. We do not already have the Skopelos-Town Πλάκα (only one Πλάκ* name exists in our Skopelos data; nearest record to the OSM coord is Γλυστέρι ~2 km away), so it is a real distinct beach we are missing. Name collides with our existing southwest Πλάκα, so disambiguated as the Chora/town beach.
